cohort: Pregnant women hospitalized for liver dysfunction in late pregnancy between 2010-2012 (observation group) and pregnant women with normal liver function during the same period (control group)
finding: Liver dysfunction in late pregnancy, particularly with severe transaminase increase, was associated with an increased risk of adverse maternal events.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were higher in the observation group and the severe transaminase increase group compared to the control group.
